current.text: He opted into a 1-year, 49 million USD contract after he could not find a new team. It is the final year of his deal, and the Kings have no interest in extending him.
He is a projected starter, with Acuff, Murray, Simmons and Sabonis.
He is expected to start and play 30+ minutes.
Schroder, Westbrook and DeRozan are gone, so he shares the ball mainly with Sabonis.
Ham calls him the Kings' second best player behind Sabonis.
Experts expect more usage and ball handling than last season, when he was used as a spot-up shooter. His assists could rise a lot with better shooters around him and better luck.
A trade or buyout is possible during the season. The Kings could also bench him or cut his minutes because they are focused on the future.
Experts say the Kings' unpredictable rotations and unclear plans for him hold back his value.
Experts disagree on the Kings' direction. One expects them to trade or sit veterans and finish near the bottom. Others expect them to keep trying to win to stay out of the relegation zone.
Yahoo lists him as questionable (Rest). A note also mentions a finger injury.
His draft position is rising fast in mock drafts. He went around pick 120 early in draft season and now goes between about 85 and 97.

Experts call him one of the best Kings targets and are happy to draft him inside the top 100. They are not worried about the finger injury. He could be a top-80 player and should beat his ranking per game, but the Kings situation makes him risky.
Kings playoff schedule for a March 28 end: 4-4-3, 11 games in weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: Threes and points are his best categories.
Experts call his shooting elite: elite FT%, elite FG% for his position and a good 3P%.
He can add around 4.5 assists when he has the ball. His assists drop when others handle it.
He is a poor defender and is 31.

note: The sites price him low (Yahoo 4 USD value, 1.8 USD average cost, ESPN 1.5 USD), but his mock draft position has jumped from about 120 to 85-97, and he cost 12 USD in our league last season. Expect to pay around 5 to 12 USD for a scorer who brings threes, points and good percentages with no flagged weak category, so he fits most builds. Early on, check whether his assists and usage rise with the ball in his hands, watch for trade or buyout news, and see if the Kings keep him near 30+ minutes after his 39-game 2025-26 season.
